title: Modular Pilot Pricing and Security Decision Kit
author: Sana Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document is a compact, modular primer for sales engineers and account teams running technical pilots with platform and security stakeholders. It bundles positioning language, a concise competitive brief, a 10-slide pitch deck outline with speaker notes, pragmatic pricing scenarios, an operational pilot checklist, a compact customer case study, and a scoped security FAQ tailored to procurement/CISO workflows. Use this as the single-page decision kit during pilot planning and executive briefings.

Audience
- Platform engineers and SREs evaluating inference economics and operational controls
- Security, compliance, and procurement stakeholders reviewing risk and evidence
- Sales engineers and solution architects running pilots and creating proposals

Key messages (one-liners by buyer persona)
- Platform engineer: "Predictable throughput, telemetry-first rollout, and consistent latency across hosted, reserved, and private deployments."
- Product manager / ML engineer: "Ship LLM features with measurable unit economics — trade latency for cost with config-level controls and regression alerts."
- CISO / Security lead: "Private deployment options, tenant isolation, KMS-backed keys, and auditable runtime logs with role-based controls."

Competitive briefing (90-second digest)
- Competitors in typical deals: GenericCloudAI, EdgeInferenceCo, ModelHoster.
- Strengths to call out: unified runtime across environments, cost-control levers (batching, cache, quantization profiles), automated fallback routing, and first-class audit/rollout features.
- Typical competitor gaps to highlight: poor multi-environment parity, opaque per-token economics, no automated KV/prefix caching, limited private deployment options or complex lift-and-shift.
- Battle-tested differentiators to assert:
  - Transparent per-token and per-route cost breakdowns in Redwood Console
  - Canary + automatic fallback policies built-in (no custom infra required)
  - Dedicated commit options that guarantee tail latency SLOs (configured per-model class)

Pitch deck outline (10 slides) — speaker notes included
1) Title / ask
   - Note: 1-sentence problem + one-line ask (pilot scope + target success metric).
2) Problem statement (latency, cost, reliability fragmentation)
   - Note: Use a real example (NPS hit, checkout friction, search latency).
3) Redwood solution in 30 seconds (hosted, dedicated, private + unified API)
   - Note: Emphasize consistent dev experience and migration path.
4) Technical architecture (runtime, smart router, KV caching)
   - Note: Simple diagram: client -> smart router -> pool (hosted | dedicated | private) -> serving runtime.
5) Pilot plan summary (scope, timeline, success metrics)
   - Note: 6–8 week pilot preferred; show acceptance criteria.
6) Pricing and cost control levers (sample math)
   - Note: Include sample cost run for expected QPS and tokens/session.
7) Security and compliance summary (evidence and options)
   - Note: Highlight private deploy, KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO status.
8) Competitive delta (3-box comparison)
   - Note: Call out unique runtime features and operational visibility.
9) Customer evidence (one short case study and metrics)
   - Note: Use anonymized metric: 35% cost per inference reduction, 2x sustained throughput.
10) Next steps and ask (POC kick-off checklist)
   - Note: Be explicit about needed access, timeline, and commercial anchor (trial credits or reserved commit).

Pricing guidance (pragmatic scenarios)
- Pricing model building blocks (definitions):
  - Hosted API: per-token generation (prompt + completion) and per-embedding unit charges.
  - Dedicated: monthly reserved GPU pool (commit tiers) + overage per-token at discounted rates.
  - Private: platform license (annual) + optional deployment and support fees.
- Representative rates (example only; substitute with negotiated margins):
  - Hosted generation: $0.0035 per 1K tokens (prompt + completion combined)
  - Embeddings: $0.004 per 1K embedding units
  - Dedicated commit: $40,000 / GPU-month (baseline for 80A-class instance pool); discounted per-token at $0.0018 per 1K tokens beyond commit utilization
  - Private license: $120,000 / year base platform fee + deployment engineering (one-time) $45,000
- Example scenario: Chat search pilot (estimates)
  - Assumptions: 25 QPS sustained (peak 45), 150 tokens per request average, 30-day pilot at 10% peak load average utilization.
  - Hosted cost estimate: 25 QPS * 150 tokens * 3600 * 24 * 30 = ~9.72B tokens/month. At $0.0035/1K = $34,020/month.
  - Dedicated reserve: Reserve 4 x 80A GPUs = $160,000/month commit (sample). If utilization >65% this yields lower per-token economics; show per-token and payback in slide.
- Pricing playbook principles:
  1. Start with a small hosted pilot to validate metrics and data flows.
  2. Use usage profile from pilot to model dedicated commit; show 3- and 12-month ROI.
  3. Offer a capped overage during pilot to limit buyer risk.
  4. For enterprise deals, bundle observability retention and priority SLAs under an uplift.

Pilot-to-production checklist (operational, 8 items)
1) Kick-off: Confirm pilot scope, data residency and sample data, success metrics and timeline (owner: SE)
2) Access: Provision API keys, SSO test account, and networking (owner: Customer infra & Redwood SE)
3) Instrumentation: Install tracing hooks and token-level metrics in the app (owner: Platform eng)
4) Baseline measurement: Capture current latency, cost per call, and error rates (owner: Customer SRE)
5) Pilot deployment: Run canary with 5% traffic for 3 days, validate latencies and traces (owner: Redwood SE)
6) Security review: Exchange pen-test artifacts, configure KMS and audit log retention (owner: Customer security)
7) Scale test: Synthetic load to 2x expected peak for 4 hours, check autoscaling and fallbacks (owner: Redwood SRE)
8) Acceptance and handoff: Document runbook, SLO targets, and next steps for Dedicated/Private procurement (owner: Customer Product + Redwood AM)

Acceptance criteria (examples)
- Median generation latency < 250ms for core path at 95th percentile under production-shaped load
- Cost per 1K tokens within 15% of pilot estimate
- No blocked calls due to auth/networking for >72 hours of pilot runtime

Customer case study (compact)
- Customer: LedgerPay (anonymized fintech)
- Problem: High-latency document summarization impacting agent throughput; costs spiraled as queries scaled.
- Approach: 6-week pilot using Hosted + KV prefix caching and model quantization suggestions.
- Outcome: 40% reduction in average latency (from 310ms -> 186ms at 95th percentile), 32% lower inference spend per produced summary, and a successful procurement of a 6-month dedicated commit after validation.
- Why it mattered: Lower latency unlocked real-time agent assist flows, reducing average handle time and improving user satisfaction metrics used in the contract renewal.

Security FAQ (targeted questions from CISO/procurement)
Q: Where does customer data reside during inference?
A: Data residency options: hosted regions (US, EU, APAC) with selectable region policy; Dedicated and Private keep data in customer VPC/cluster by design.

Q: Do you offer customer-managed keys?
A: Yes. Private and Dedicated options support KMS/HSM integration. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys with optional Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) in configured regions.

Q: What audit and observability artifacts are available?
A: Per-request traces, token-level cost breakdowns, model version and route metadata, audit logs for API key activity, and retention configuration (90/365/retention-by-contract).

Q: How is PII handled and deleted?
A: We support configurable retention windows and a deletion API. For Private deployments, data never leaves the customer-controlled environment; for Hosted, we can configure strict retention and redaction pipelines as part of an enterprise contract.

Q: What certifications and third-party assurance do you have?
A: Current baseline: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 (evidence available under NDA). Pen tests are scheduled quarterly and results summary is available to signed customers.

Q: Network and segmentation controls?
A: Private deployments use customer VPCs and can be air-gapped. Dedicated pools are logically isolated; we provide peering/VPN instructions and IP allowlists.

Q: How do you handle model updates and rollouts securely?
A: Rollouts are controlled via canary policies and automatic fallback to previous model variants on error or quality regressions. All rollout events are recorded in the audit log and tied to an operator identity.

Q: Incident response and escalation?
A: Enterprise customers get a named security contact, 24/7 on-call for sev-1 security incidents, and runbook-driven triage. For hosted customers we publish status updates through the Redwood status page and offer paid incident SLA add-ons.

Appendix: sample API snippet (quick sanity check)
- cURL example (streaming generation):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $PILOT_KEY'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-1","input":"Summarize customer transcript","max_tokens":256}'

Cost estimation JSON example (paste into spreadsheet)
{
  "qps": "25",
  "avg_tokens": "150",
  "days": "30",
  "hosted_rate_per_1k_tokens": "0.0035"
}

References and next steps
- Recommended: Run the 6-week hosted pilot; capture token-level billing and trace exports in week 1.
- If pilot economics validate, model a 3-month dedicated commit with a capped overage and an observability retention uplift.
